doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Receiving the NEA Jazz Masters award in New York
summary: Young recalls going to New York in the fall to receive the award and the struggle to name fellow recipients.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: So, here we are in 2009, last year…last year he received a NEA, in 2008 [speaking to Mr. Kimery], that‘s what I got here.
Uh-hm.
So you received your NEA Jazz Masters…Jazz Masters…NEA Jazz Masters Award.
What about it, what did you say?
You received it last year.
Yeah, I was on it last year, in like October/November, right in there someplace, onetime. What was it?
You received the Jazz Masters Award, was it in January? [speaking to Mr. Kimery]
No, I went to New York, to the…
New York, yeah, in October.
Oh, so just recently?
Yeah.
Ok, alright.
I went to New York for…
To get the award?
Yeah, to get the award, and that was like…October or November, right in there someplace.
How was that? How did you feel about receiving that award? How did you feel about being, receiving the award?

Well, I was surprised to get it because after awhile they wait until I‘m ninety years old [laughs]. No, I‘m just kidding. But it was very nice, man, I really appreciated getting the award. I got it, lets see, there was…what‘s that trumpet player‘s name? He got it, me…and the trombone player. Have you got the list of the names of the men who did it this year, who got the award?
It was…
The trumpet player, the trombone player…the trumpet player is…oh heck, he‘s a young cat but...oh man, I wish you had the names of that…
Yeah, I wish I did, too.
Well, George Benson got it.
Huh?
George Benson…
George Benson, guitarist, George Benson got it.
George Benson? Yeah, he was one. George Benson, yeah, George Benson. Isn‘t that something, we can‘t think of these people‘s names.
All of us got memory loss.
Jimmy Cobb.
Oh, Jimmy Cobb.
Jimmy Cobb, Jimmy Cobb.
Yeah, the records…reengineer, did all the stuff in Hoboken.
Oh, Rudy Van Gelder.
Rudy Van Gelder.
Who?
Rudy Van Gelder.
Rudy Van Gelder, well, he had a club, I mean he had a…
Recording studio. Young:…recording studio way in New Jersey. Rudy Van Gelder, myself, the guitar player…
George Benson, Jimmy Cobb…
The trumpet player…
White or black? White or black, the trumpet player, was he white or black?
He‘s black.
Black, younger than you. Young, no, older, older cat. Who is even up, I can‘t even think of any trumpet players who…I‘m just thinking like Clark Terry, but it wouldn‘t have been him.
No, it wasn‘t Clark Terry. He‘s a trumpet player around your age.
Oh, really.
Yeah, I‘m drawing a blank here.
Yeah, if he‘s getting a Jazz Masters Award he should be older than me. But anyway, you felt good about the award, you felt good to get the award?
